column2: On the authority of the Mother of the Believers, Umm ʿAbdillāh ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: The Messenger of Allah (Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace) said: “Whoever introduces into this matter of ours what is not part of it, it is rejected.” Reported by al-Bukhārī and Muslim.
In a narration of Muslim: “Whoever does a deed that is not in accordance with our matter, it is rejected.”
“Into this matter of ours”: our religion.
“What is not part of it”: of the religion, in that nothing among the proofs of the Sharīʿah or its general principles supports it.
Radd (“rejected”): thrown back, not accepted; a verbal noun used in the sense of a passive participle.

The rejection of every newly introduced matter in the religion that does not conform to the Sharīʿah. The second narration states explicitly that every newly introduced matter is to be abandoned, whether its doer introduced it or was preceded in it; for some obstinate people, when they practise an innovation, argue:

“I did not introduce anything”, and so the second narration is used as an argument against them: “Whoever does a deed that is not in accordance with our matter, it is rejected.” This hadith should be memorised and used in refuting objectionable things.
Whatever is supported by anything among the proofs of the Sharīʿah or its general principles is not rejected; rather, it is accepted.
All prohibited contracts are void, and the results that would follow from them do not come into existence.
A prohibition entails invalidity, because all prohibited things are not part of the matter of the religion and so must be rejected.
The judgement of a judge does not change the inner reality of a matter, because he said, “that is not in accordance with our matter”, by which he meant the religion.
An invalid settlement is annulled, and what is taken under it must be returned.
